dashboard.title: Dashboard
projects.heading: Projects
language.label: Language
refused.unauthenticated.title: Sign-in required
refused.unauthenticated.body: Dockyard can only be reached through its authentication proxy. Open it from the address your Administrator gave you.
refused.not_invited.title: Not invited
refused.not_invited.body: The email {email} has been verified by the authentication proxy, but it has not been invited to this Dockyard Instance. Ask an Administrator to invite you.
refused.identity_unavailable.title: Identity cannot be verified
refused.identity_unavailable.body: Dockyard cannot verify who you are right now, because it cannot reach the authentication proxy. Try again in a few minutes; if it keeps happening, tell your Administrator.
not_found.title: Page not found
claude_account.heading: Claude Account
claude_account.explain: Your Projects work with your claude.ai subscription (Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise). Connect it once: Dockyard opens a terminal where you sign in.
claude_account.warning: Sign in with your claude.ai subscription only. Do not use an API key or a long-lived token (such as one made with claude setup-token): they disable Remote Control, and your Projects would not appear in the Claude app.
sign_in.title: Connect your Claude Account
sign_in.step_open: Open the link shown in the terminal and sign in with your claude.ai account.
sign_in.step_copy: Copy the code claude.ai shows you at the end.
sign_in.step_paste: Paste it below and send it, or type it in the terminal and press Enter.
sign_in.not_connected: The sign-in ended without connecting your Claude Account. Check the messages in the terminal, then try again from the dashboard.
sign_in.lost: The connection to the terminal was lost. Reload the page to see it again: the sign-in keeps waiting for you.
refused.cross_site.title: Refused: sent by another site
refused.cross_site.body: This request reached Dockyard from another site, so it was refused: only pages of Dockyard itself can act on your behalf. If you were using Dockyard at its usual address, tell your Administrator: the proxy in front of Dockyard must pass the original Host header through.
refused.outside_local_networks.title: Not reachable
refused.outside_local_networks.body: This address is not reachable from your network.
runtime_unavailable.title: Docker is unreachable
runtime_unavailable.body: Dockyard cannot reach Docker right now, so it can neither check your Claude Account nor run your Projects. Try again in a few minutes; if it keeps happening, tell your Administrator: the details are in Dockyard's log.
project_refused.repository_invalid.body: This is not the address of a repository. Use https://github.com/owner/repository or https://gitlab.com/group/project, as your browser shows it on the repository's page.
project_refused.repository_not_https.bod: Use the repository's https:// address, for example https://github.com/owner/repository. Other kinds of address, such as http:// or git@, are not accepted.
project_refused.repository_credentials.b: Remove the user name and password (or token) from the address: Dockyard never takes credentials in a URL.
project_refused.repository_port.body: Remove the port from the address: only the standard https port is accepted.
project_refused.repository_query.body: Remove everything from the ? onwards: the address of a repository has no query.
project_refused.repository_fragment.body: Remove everything from the # onwards: the address of a repository has no fragment.
project_refused.repository_host.body: Only repositories on github.com and gitlab.com are supported.
project_refused.name_missing.body: Give the Project a name: it becomes the name of its Remote Control Server in the Claude app.
project_refused.name_invalid.body: Use a name of at most 60 characters, on one line.
project_new.title: New Project
project_new.repository_hint: The https:// address of a repository on github.com or gitlab.com, for example https://github.com/owner/repository.
project_new.name: Name
project_new.name_hint: It becomes the name of its Remote Control Server in the Claude app, so you recognise it on your phone.
project_new.public_hint: Anyone can clone a public repository, so it needs no Git Credential: add one only if Claude should open issues and pull requests or push.
project.cloning: Dockyard is cloning the repository; this page follows its progress.
project.error: Something is wrong with this Project: its Remote Control Server keeps stopping, or its code is missing. Restart it; if that does not help, check that your Claude Account is connected, or delete the Project and create it again.
project.delete.heading: Delete this Project
project.delete.explain: Deleting removes the Project and its environment. Its code and home folder are kept unless you choose to delete them too.
project.delete.code: Also delete its code and its home folder: they cannot be recovered
clone_failed.title: The clone failed
clone_failed.explain: Git could not clone {repository}. Nothing was kept: the Project has been removed, so you can simply try again.
project_refused.cloning.body: This Project is still being cloned: wait until the clone ends, then start it.
project_new.permission_mode_hint: How much Claude may do in this Project without asking you first.
permission_mode.default_hint: Claude asks before editing files or running commands.
permission_mode.acceptEdits_hint: Claude edits files without asking, and asks before running commands.
permission_mode.auto_hint: Claude decides by itself which actions are safe to take without asking.
permission_mode.bypassPermissions_hint: Claude never asks: it edits any file and runs any command.
permission_mode.bypass_warning: Only for repositories you fully trust. Claude will run any command without asking you, including whatever the repository's files tell it to do. The Project stays cut off from your other Projects, but it reaches the internet and works with your Claude Account.
project.running: Open the Claude app, Code tab: this Project appears there as “{name}”.
project.sessions: The first Session works directly in the main checkout, on the branch that was cloned. Every additional Session you open gets its own git worktree, so Sessions working in parallel do not step on each other.
project.waiting: This Project starts by itself as soon as your Claude Account is connected.
project.stopped: The Remote Control Server is stopped: the Project does not appear in the Claude app.
project_refused.not_running.body: This Project is not running: start it first.
project.trust_prompt: The Remote Control Server asks whether to trust this Project's folder, and waits for an answer: until then the Project does not appear in the Claude app. Open the console and choose “Yes, I trust this folder”.
project.cpu_hint: 100% is one full CPU; this Project may use {cpus}.
logs.title: Log
logs.explain: What the Remote Control Server prints, as it prints it, starting with its last 1000 lines.
logs.terminal: Log of the Remote Control Server
console.title: Console
console.explain: The Remote Control Server's own screen, live: answer here what it asks, such as whether to trust this Project's folder.
console.ctrl_c: Careful: Ctrl+C in the console stops the Remote Control Server, and with it the Sessions open in the Claude app. It starts again by itself, but those Sessions are interrupted.
console.terminal: Console of the Remote Control Server
console.answer_hint: Sent followed by Enter; leave it empty to press Enter alone.
stream.ended: The Remote Control Server stopped or restarted. Reload the page to follow it again.
stream.not_running: This Project is not running: start it from its page.
stream.lost: The connection was lost. Reload the page to follow the Remote Control Server again.
terminal.title: Terminal
terminal.explain: A shell in this Project's folder, as its non-root user: run git, gh, glab or Claude Code (claude, or claude --remote-control). Ctrl+C here stops only what the shell runs.
terminal.leave: Leaving this page closes the shell and ends whatever runs in it.
terminal.command_hint: Sent followed by Enter, handy on a phone; leave it empty to press Enter alone.
terminal.ended: The shell ended: it exited, or the Project stopped or restarted. Reload the page to open a new one.
terminal.lost: The connection was lost, and the shell with it. Reload the page to open a new one.
git_credential_refused.label_missing.bod: Give the Git Credential a label, so you recognise it when you choose it for a Project.
git_credential_refused.label_invalid.bod: Use a label of at most 60 characters, on one line.
git_credential_refused.token_missing.bod: Paste the token GitHub or GitLab gave you.
git_credential_refused.token_invalid.bod: This does not look like a GitHub or GitLab token: paste it exactly as the provider showed it, with no spaces or other text around it.
git_credentials.heading: Git Credentials
git_credentials.explain: Your GitHub and GitLab access tokens, reusable across your Projects. Once saved, a token is stored encrypted and never shown again.
git_credentials.empty: You have no Git Credentials yet.
git_credential.risk: Claude can read this token inside the Projects that use it, and so can any code from the repository that runs there (scripts, tests, dependencies): whatever the token allows, they can do.
git_credential.scopes: So give it as little as possible:
git_credential.scopes_github: GitHub: a fine-grained personal access token, limited to the repositories Claude works on, with an expiry date and only the permissions it needs: Contents and Pull requests (read and write), Issues if Claude opens them.
git_credential.scopes_gitlab: GitLab: a project or group access token (or a personal one) with an expiry date, the Developer role and only the scopes it needs: api to work on issues, merge requests and pipelines with glab, or just read_repository and write_repository if Claude only pulls and pushes.
git_credential_new.title: Add a Git Credential
git_credential.label: Label
git_credential.label_hint: Your name for it, such as the account or organisation it belongs to.
git_credential.token_hint: It is stored encrypted and never shown again, not even to you.
git_credential.token_saved: The token is saved, encrypted, and is never shown again: to change it, replace it.
git_credential.changed.label: The label has been changed.
git_credential.rotate.heading: Replace the token
git_credential.rotate.explain: Paste the new token: it takes the place of the saved one. Then revoke the old token on {provider}.
git_credential.delete.heading: Delete this Git Credential
git_credential.delete.explain: Dockyard forgets the token. It stays valid on {provider} until you revoke it there.
A private repository can only be cloned with a Git Credential: choose one of your Git Credentials for it, or add one first from the dashboard.
project_refused.git_credential_not_found: This Git Credential does not exist: choose one of yours from the list.
Choose a Git Credential of the repository's provider: a GitHub one for github.com, a GitLab one for gitlab.com.
project_refused.cpus_out_of_range.body: Choose between {min_cpus} and {max_cpus} CPUs: that is what a Project may use on this Instance.
project_refused.memory_out_of_range.body: Choose between {min_memory} and {max_memory} GiB of RAM: that is what a Project may use on this Instance.
project_refused.active_maximum.title: Too many Active Projects
project_refused.active_maximum.body: You have reached the maximum of Active Projects this Instance allows each User ({max_active}): stop one of them first. A stopped Project keeps its code and home folder.
project_new.resources_hint: The most this Project may use. Active Projects you may have at once: {max_active}.
project_new.cpus_hint: Between {min_cpus} and {max_cpus}; {max_cpus} unless you choose less.
project_new.memory_hint: Between {min_memory} and {max_memory} GiB; {max_memory} unless you choose less.
project.resources_value: CPUs up to {cpus}, RAM up to {memory} GiB
git_credential_in_use.body: This Git Credential is used by these Projects: {projects}. Delete them first, then delete the Git Credential.
git_credential.in_use_refused: This Git Credential cannot be deleted: the Projects listed below use it. Delete them first.
git_credential.delete.in_use: It cannot be deleted while Projects use it. Delete these Projects first:
git_credential.rotate.next_start: The Projects using it receive the new token at their next start: restart those that are running.
project_new.private_hint: Dockyard clones a private repository with one of your Git Credentials.
project_new.git_credential_hint: Dockyard clones with it, and Claude uses it inside the Project with gh, glab and git push. Required for a private repository; only Git Credentials of the repository's provider are offered.
project_new.no_git_credentials: You have no Git Credentials yet: a private Project needs one.
project.git_credential_inside: Dockyard hands its token to the Project at every start: a token you replace reaches the Project at its next start.
administrator_only.title: Administrators only
administrator_only.body: Only an Administrator can do this. Ask one of the Administrators of this Instance.
invitation_refused.email_invalid.body: This is not an email address: write it in full, such as name@example.com.
invitation_refused.already_user.body: This person is already a User of this Instance.
invitation_refused.already_invited.body: This email is already invited: the Invitation waits for the person's first access.
last_administrator.title: The last Administrator
last_administrator.body: This is the last Administrator of the Instance: it cannot be demoted or removed, or nobody could manage the Instance. Promote another User first.
administration.heading: Administration
administration.explain: Invite people, choose who can use and manage this Instance, define the Images Projects run in, and look after every Project on it.
users.title: Users
users.heading: Users
users.invite.heading: Invite someone
users.invite.hint: The email they sign in with through the authentication proxy, which must let them through too. Dockyard sends no message: tell them the address of this Instance. They become a User the first time they open it.
users.invitations.heading: Pending Invitations
users.invitations.empty: No Invitations are waiting for a first access.
user.role.heading: Role
user.role.administrator: An Administrator manages the Instance: Users, Invitations, limits and dangerous settings, besides their own Projects.
user.role.user: A User works on their own Projects, and cannot manage the Instance.
user.remove.heading: Remove this User
user.remove.explain: Removing them refuses their next request and deletes everything they own on this Instance: their Projects, with their code and home folder, their Git Credentials and their Claude Account. It cannot be undone.
user.remove.confirm: I understand that this cannot be undone
user.remove.unconfirmed: Tick the box to confirm: removing a User cannot be undone.
all_projects.title: All Projects
all_projects.heading: All Projects
all_projects.explain: Every Project on this Instance. Stop or delete any of them to free resources or stop abuse: deleting keeps its code and home folder unless you choose otherwise. Its Terminal, console and logs stay private to its User.
all_projects.empty: There are no Projects on this Instance yet.
project_refused.privileged_not_permitted: Only a User an Administrator has granted the Privileged Projects permission can create or start a Privileged Project. Ask an Administrator if you need one.
privileged.warning: A Privileged Project equals root on the host. Whatever runs in it, Claude or the repository's own code, can take over the whole machine and read every User's code, Git Credentials and Claude Account. Use it only when you need it, for example to run Docker inside the Project, and only with repositories you fully trust.
project_new.privileged_confirm: Run this Project privileged: I understand that it equals root on the host
user.privileged.heading: Privileged Projects
user.privileged.explain: Grant this only to someone you would give root on this machine. Revoking it stops their Privileged Projects, which cannot start again until it is granted again.
images.title: Images
images.heading: Images
images.explain: Users pick one of the ready Images when they create a Project. Each one is the Base Image plus the build instructions you write: Dockyard builds it, then checks that Claude Code is in it and that it does not run as root.
images.base.label: Base Image
images.base.description: Claude Code, git, gh, glab, Node and Python.
image_new.title: New Image
image_new.label: Label
image_new.label_hint: What Users see when they pick it, for example Rust or Data science.
image_new.description_hint: What it adds to the Base Image, so that Users know when to pick it. Optional.
image_new.instructions_hint: Only what to add: Dockerfile instructions such as RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y ripgrep. Dockyard puts them on top of the Base Image and runs them as root, then switches back to the non-root user Projects run as. Do not start with FROM.
image.building: Dockyard is building this Image, then it will check it. This can take a few minutes.
image.ready: Ready: Users can pick this Image when they create a Project.
image.failure.build: The build failed: the log below says why. Fix the instructions in a new Image, then delete this one.
image.failure.claude_missing: Built, but Claude Code is missing from it, so Projects could not run in it. Users cannot pick it.
image.failure.root_user: Built, but its default user is root, so Users cannot pick it: Projects run as the non-root user of the Base Image.
image.base_explain: The Base Image ships with Dockyard, and every other Image is built on top of it. It is always available and cannot be deleted.
image.delete.heading: Delete this Image
image.delete.explain: It can be deleted only while no Project uses it.
image.delete.in_use: It cannot be deleted while Projects use it. These Projects use it:
image.in_use_refused: This Image cannot be deleted: the Projects listed below use it.
image_refused.label_missing.body: Give the Image a label: Users pick it by its label.
image_refused.label_invalid.body: Use a label of at most 60 characters, on one line.
image_refused.description_invalid.body: Use a description of at most 500 characters.
image_refused.instructions_missing.body: Write the build instructions to add to the Base Image, for example RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y ripgrep.
image_refused.instructions_invalid.body: The build instructions are too long (at most 20,000 characters) or hold characters that are not text.
image_refused.instructions_from.body: Remove the FROM instruction: Dockyard always builds on top of the Base Image, which has what Projects need (Claude Code and the non-root user).
image_in_use.body: This Image is used by these Projects: {projects}. They must be deleted first, then the Image can be deleted.
base_image.body: The Base Image ships with Dockyard: it cannot be deleted.
project_refused.image_not_available.body: This Image cannot be picked: it is not ready, or it was deleted. Pick one of the Images offered on the new Project form.
project_new.image_hint: What the Project's Claude Code has to work with: the Base Image, or one an Administrator prepared with more tools.
project_refused.not_stopped.body: Stop this Project first: its Image can change only while it is stopped.
base_image_not_built.title: The Base Image is not built by Dockyard
base_image_not_built.body: The Base Image ships with Dockyard: it is updated with Dockyard itself (docker compose pull), and every other Image is then built again on top of it.
image_building.title: Already building
image_building.body: This Image is being built already: wait until its build ends.
project.update_available: A newer build of its Image is ready. Restart it to move to the newer build: its code and home folder stay.
project.change_image.heading: Change Image
project.change_image.explain: The Project starts in the Image you pick from its next start on, and keeps its code and home folder.
project.change_image.stop_first: Stop the Project to change its Image: its code and home folder stay.
image.previous_build: Projects using this Image keep starting from its previous build, which passed its check, until a new build does.
image.rebuild.explain: Build it again from its instructions, on top of the Base Image as it is now. Projects keep starting from the build they have until the new one is ready.
administration.failed_images: These Images failed to build: Users cannot pick them. Open each one to see why.
local_sign_in.title: Sign in
local_sign_in.explain: Local sign-in: use the email and the password you have on this Dockyard.
local_sign_in.refused: The email or the password is wrong.
local_sign_in.slowed_down.seconds: Too many failed attempts. Try again in {seconds} s.
local_sign_in.slowed_down.minutes: Too many failed attempts. Try again in {minutes} min.
local_sign_in.required.title: Sign-in required
activate.title: Choose your password
activate.explain: You are invited to this Dockyard as {email}. Choose the password you will sign in with here.
activate.rules: At least 12 characters, and not your email.
activate.submit: Set the password and sign in
activate.refused.too_short: The password is too short: it needs at least 12 characters.
activate.refused.equals_email: The password cannot be your email.
activation_link_invalid.title: Activation link not valid
activation_link_invalid.body: This Activation link has expired, was already used or was replaced by a new one. Ask an Administrator for a new one.
users.invite.hint_local: Dockyard sends no message: hand them the Activation link you get here, with which they choose their password on the local address. If the authentication proxy also lets them through, whichever they use first makes them a User.
users.activation_link.label: Activation link for {email}
users.activation_link.hint: Hand it over yourself, through a channel you trust: whoever has it can choose the password. It works once, for 7 days, and is shown only now; make a new one if it gets lost.
users.activation_link.hint_reset: Hand it over yourself, through a channel you trust: whoever has it can choose a new password for this User, which signs them out everywhere. It works once, for 7 days, and is shown only now; make a new one if it gets lost.
activate.reset.title: Choose a new password
activate.reset.explain: Choose a new password for {email}. Once it is set, you are signed out everywhere else.
own_page.password.heading: Password
own_page.password.none: You have no password yet. Set one to sign in on the local address too, with your email and that password.
own_page.password.set: You have a password: you can sign in on the local address with your email and that password.
own_page.password.change_locally: To change it, open this page on the local address and give the current password.
own_page.password.saved: Your password is saved. Your other sign-in sessions are signed out.
own_page.password.already_set: You already have a password: it changes only by giving it, on the local address.
own_page.second_factor.heading: Second factor
own_page.second_factor.on: You have a Second factor: on the local address, after the password, you also give a code from your authenticator app.
own_page.second_factor.off: You have no Second factor: on the local address, the password alone signs you in. Turn one on to be asked for a code from an authenticator app too.
own_page.second_factor.change_locally: To turn it on or off, open this page on the local address.
own_page.second_factor.new_recovery_code: New recovery codes void the ones you have.
own_page.second_factor.code_or_password: Code from your authenticator app, or your password
own_page.second_factor.wrong: The code or the password is wrong.
second_factor.title: Turn on the Second factor
second_factor.scan: Scan this QR code with your authenticator app.
second_factor.qr_code: QR code for your authenticator app
second_factor.type: Or type this secret into it:
second_factor.hint: The Second factor takes effect only once this code is right.
second_factor.refused: The code is wrong: check your phone's clock, then try the code the app shows now.
recovery_codes.title: Your recovery codes
recovery_codes.explain: Each code signs you in once, in place of a code from your authenticator app. Store them somewhere safe: they are shown only now.
local_sign_in.code.title: Enter your code
local_sign_in.code.explain: You have a Second factor: enter the code your authenticator app shows now.
local_sign_in.code.hint: Or one of your recovery codes, if you do not have the app at hand.
local_sign_in.code.over: The time to enter the code ran out, or the code was already given. Sign in again.
